entities.summary: Nikolai Viktorovich Nasonov was a Russian and Soviet zoologist. In 1879 he graduated from the Imperial Moscow University and became an assistant at its Zoological Museum. After defending his PhD in 1887 he lectured at his alma mater, and later worked in Trieste, Marseille and Warsaw. In 1890 he defended a habilitation on the evolution of ants. In December 1897 he was elected as a corresponding and in March 1906 as a full member of the Russian Academy of Sciences. In addition to his studies in zoology Nasonov also dealt with the race problem based on Marxism and published articles in Revolutsionnyi vostok, a monthly journal published by the Communist University of the Toilers of the East.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Nasonov's work on the evolution of ants and his involvement with Marxist ideology had a regional impact in Eastern Europe, particularly through his association with the Communist University of the Toilers of the East. His contributions to zoology also contributed to the development of scientific knowledge in Russia.
